summary: The app's own sketch solver no longer reports freedom as unknown for sketches whose rank is clear but whose rank factor looks ill conditioned, such as a two-link arm stretched nearly straight, and no longer calls rank clear on an estimate that can miss a weak direction. Rank is clear only when the independent rows are shown to have a smallest singular value of at least 1e-7. Before, that value was estimated by four inverse iterations over the factor's pivot columns. An estimate approaches from above, so a weak direction it nearly missed could be called clear and the sketch's freedom and short-decimal rounding applied; leaving out the columns without pivots also made a nearly straight arm's rank falsely unclear, since its second link leaves a tiny lead in the joint's columns. Now a lower bound over the pivot columns decides first, since leaving out columns can only lower the rows' own value. One bound, from the comparison matrix of their triangle, costs two passes over it; when entries of the triangle's inverse cancel it is too low, and one over the Frobenius norm of that inverse, at most the square root of the rank below the true value, is tried next. Otherwise the singular values of the independent rows themselves are computed: those of S in the transposed factorization R^T = Q S, built by the same rotations as the witness fit within the group's fill limit, and taken densely, accurate to about epsilon absolutely, for groups of at most 32 independent rows; rank is clear when the smallest reaches 1e-7. Larger groups, or a factor that would pass the fill limit, leave rank unclear. The checks past the comparison bound take at most 64 million counted entries, 20 million of them for the inverse, and half the work left, so the solve and the rest of the diagnosis keep the remainder; past that rank stays unclear rather than the diagnosis unavailable. The same rule, within the group's fill limit, decides which rows are set aside before a group's first solve, and is not applied when none would be. The dense step costs up to about 41 million counted entries of the 400 million work allowance for 30 rows. In native release builds, solving 3,200 chained midpoints, staircases of 200 to 2,000 steps and 5,000 links takes as long as before. Sketches at a real tangency still solve with freedom unknown, and drags onto one still stop short of it.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Some sketches that showed freedom as unknown now show their freedom, and a sketch whose rank only an estimate called clear now shows freedom as unknown and keeps its values unrounded. No protocol change.

checklist.verification: The Rust arm test now requires every one of its 47 frames, from the start and chained, and the ordinary solve after each, to be diagnosed with freedom 2; three frames from the start and three chained were uncertain before. The tangency drags for radii 10, 100 and 1000 still end limited, the sketches they leave still solve with rank uncertain, a repeated distance beside a near tangency is still redundant, and a weakly held direction is still uncertain. Three rows whose singular values are about 1.7, 1.2e-7 and 1e-8, built so that an inverse iteration from a fixed start nearly misses the weakest direction, stay uncertain. Three nearly parallel rows whose leads all pass 1e-10, and whose smallest singular value is about 9e-9 while an inverse iteration from a fixed start estimates 1.2e-7, also stay uncertain; this failed before. Eighty rows of ones in three consecutive columns, whose comparison bound fails, are shown clear through the rows of the inverse beyond the 32 computed densely. Thirty rows with tiny pivot leads but well-conditioned entries elsewhere, sharing one column, with a repeat of the first, have the repeat set aside with no fill limit, at under 60 million counted entries, and nothing set aside when their transposed factor would pass a fill limit of 100. Twenty rows 1, 2, 2 in consecutive columns, which are clear with enough work, are diagnosed with rank unclear within a budget of 140 counted entries instead of overspending it and becoming unavailable, and before a solve with 200 their repeat is not set aside while the work spent stays under 160. For one row with a tiny lead, every budget up to 200 that yields a diagnosis or rows to set aside was spent within, since each step of the checks, rotations included, is checked before it is taken and a dense decomposition that runs out is charged all it was allowed; a point held twice on a nearly flat line solves within 27 counted entries, which ran out before. A 10,000-link chain, which ran out of work while the inverse's rows were enumerated, and 12,000 chained midpoints solve and are diagnosed. The runtime arm test requires freedom 2 on every frame. All Rust suites, the sketch-solver and benchmark Vitest suites, and the full test suite pass.

publicNotes.summary: Fewer sketches show their freedom as unknown.
changes: Shows the remaining freedom of sketches such as a nearly straight arm, which the app's own solver reported as unknown.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
